messages.subject: A question on binwidth parameter (qplot)
parts:
Hi all,

If I run the following example (next 4 lines):

library('ggplot2')
myplot <- function(mydf) { qplot(v1, data=mydf, binwidth=diff(range
(mydf$v1))/400) }
a <- data.frame(v1 = rnorm(100))
myplot(a)

... I get the following error:

Error in diff(range(mydf$v1)) : object 'mydf' not found

I've tried other variations without any success. It seems that it is
impossible to pass anything but a numeric constant as the binwidth
parameter.

Does anybody know I can pass a computed binwidth (i.e. not a
constant)? It works when the computation is done outside of the
function (at the global level) but not if the binwidth computation is
done within the function.

Thanks
Varol Kaptan

messages.author: 936ef8c6d12fc338
messages.subject: RE: A question on binwidth parameter (qplot)
parts:
Hi Varol,

It works if you use the ggplot notation instead of the qplot notation.

library('ggplot2')
myplot <- function(mydf){

ggplot(mydf, aes(x = v1)) +
geom_histogram(binwidth=diff(range(mydf$v1))/400)

}
a <- data.frame(v1 = rnorm(100))
myplot(a)
